attempted_claim: Let G* be the set of hyperbolic alternating Montesinos knots with Montesinos length at least 4, crossing number 17, 18 or 19, in which every twist region contains at most 3 crossings (low-twist, so the highly-twisted exclusion requiring at least 6 crossings per twist region does not apply). This family lies beyond the Goodman-Heard-Hodgson commensurator census to 12 crossings and the reported verification to 16 crossings. Does any complement M_K = S^3 \ K for K in G* cover a rigid-cusped orientable hyperbolic 3-orbifold with S^2(2,4,4), S^2(3,3,3) or S^2(2,3,6) cusp, including non-reflection and prism rigid cusps so that the Boileau-Boyer-Cebanu-Walsh small-reflection-orbifold theorem for AP knots does not decide it? Prove or disprove by verified commensurator-versus-normalizer computation and cusp-killing covering checks: either produce an explicit K in G* with hidden symmetries or prove every K in G* has commensurator equal to its normalizer and covers no rigid-cusped orbifold.
claim_type: existence-or-nonexistence proof over finite low-twist census
decisive_failure: No verified resolution was obtained: the alternating-knot hidden-symmetry literature shortcut could not be confirmed from primary sources, exhaustive G* enumeration timed out at millions of diagrams and tens of thousands of knot types, and rigorous snappy.verify certification requires Sage which is unavailable, leaving only single-knot floating-point heuristics.
